title: Proposal: split the Attestation component into platform evidence, identity binding and appraisal
author: imran-siddique
summary: The mission sentence in `charter.md` lists "identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization". Attestation is the only one of those with no planned deliverable in section 4, and in the Reference Architecture component list it is a single box. The part that bre...
inline_text:
The mission sentence in `charter.md` lists "identity, attestation, authentication, delegation, and authorization". Attestation is the only one of those with no planned deliverable in section 4, and in the Reference Architecture component list it is a single box. The part that breaks implementations sits inside that box.

## Where one box stops working

Hardware attestation signs over an environment. An agent identity claim needs a second link, from the agent's identity document or key to that environment, and the shape of that link differs by platform:

| Platform | How the agent's identity reaches the hardware signature |
|---|---|
| SEV-SNP via `/dev/sev-guest` (validated on GCP N2D) | Guest sets the 64-byte `REPORT_DATA` directly. One link. |
| Azure confidential VMs, SEV-SNP and TDX | `report_data` is the hash of a paravisor-built Runtime Claims JSON holding the vTPM AK public key, VM configuration and 64 bytes of `user-data` ([Microsoft design detail](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/confidential-computing/guest-attestation-confidential-virtual-machines-design)). Guest data reaches the signature only inside that structure, and the paravisor that composes it sits inside the trust boundary. |
| NVIDIA H100 GPU | A separate GPU report with its own nonce. Tying it to the CPU environment is a third link. |

We hit each of these on live deployments. On Azure, a verifier that expects `REPORT_DATA == H(identity document)` rejects valid evidence, and a verifier that checks only the hardware signature accepts evidence that says nothing about the agent.

## Proposed change

Replace the single Attestation component in the Reference Architecture with three rows:

1. **Platform evidence.** The signed hardware or firmware report and its endorsement chain. It states this environment and these measurements.
2. **Identity binding.** The signed statement tying an agent identifier or key to that evidence, through `REPORT_DATA`, runtime-claims `user-data`, or a TPM quote's `qualifyingData`. It must name who composed the binding and which components sit inside the trust boundary.
3. **Appraisal.** The relying party's verdict against its policy. An output, consistent with the appraisal label in #5.

Scope stays on the identity claims attestation can support. Secure execution belongs to Security & Privacy under section 3, and the runtime side is the Attested Isolated Runtime pattern merged in aaif/wg-security-and-privacy#26. The taxonomy definition was adopted through aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape#42; the separate proposal in aaif/ws-taxonomy-landscape#43 is now closed as superseded.

Brian Malone, as Reference Architecture coordinator, can these three rows go into the Reference Architecture working document as written? @grantdmiller @alperdedeoglu, I can walk through the Azure case at a Thursday meeting if that helps.
